title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether adding a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier (with at most one automated repair) increases the fraction of intent‑driven configuration proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic NetOps validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). For each intent we produced a single shared_initial candidate and compared: baseline — accept the single candidate; guarded — run the deterministic validator and permit at most one automated repair. Results: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and repair budget the single‑shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable marginal rescue by the guarded pipeline. All preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts are archived and the inference is explicitly conditional on the preregistered shared_initial estimand, repair budget (≤1), model, and synthetic task distribution.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being applied to operational NetOps tasks including intent→configuration translation, configuration synthesis, and automated repair. Operators require semantic guarantees—sequencing, reachability, and policy preservation—that go beyond syntactic correctness. A common mitigation architecture interposes deterministic validators and bounded automated repair in a generate→validate→repair loop to reduce risk before deployment. The measurable benefit of such guarded pipelines depends on (1) what is held fixed (the estimand), (2) the generator's single‑shot quality, (3) validator expressiveness, and (4) permitted repair budget.

We preregistered a paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) to quantify deterministic rescue when the same single LLM candidate is evaluated under two treatments. For each intent the pipeline produced one shared_initial candidate with the declared generator (gpt-5-mini) and compared: (a) baseline — accept the single candidate without repair; (b) guarded — run deterministic validation and allow at most one automated repair which itself is re‑validated. The core research question: does adding a deterministic verifier plus at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that same candidate unchanged?

Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation isolating deterministic rescue under a shared_initial estimand that conditions on a single LLM draw per intent; (2) a complete, archived execution and analysis bundle including validator traces and the single automated repair trace; (3) an artifact‑grounded discussion of ceiling effects, estimand conditioning, and operational implications for NetOps pipelines.
sections.related_work:
Surveys and recent systems work document intensive activity applying LLMs to NetOps tasks (intent translation, template synthesis, automated repair) and propose tool‑augmented agentic frameworks that call validators or external tools [https://openalex.org/W4402742293; https://openalex.org/W4411015066; https://openalex.org/W4416927413]. Empirical studies of generate→validate→repair pipelines report improvements that depend heavily on validator coverage and the allowance for resampling or iterative generation [doi:10.1609/aaai.v40i40.40676; https://openalex.org/W4404240614].

Two methodological gaps motivated our design. First, many prior comparisons conflate deterministic validator rescue with benefits produced by permitting multiple independent model draws; resampling mixes generator variance with validator effects. Second, benchmarks that emphasize semantic correctness (reachability, policy compliance) rather than syntactic validity are still emerging and vary in scope [https://openalex.org/W4415071524; https://openalex.org/W4392875514]. By conditioning on a single shared_initial draw our paired design isolates deterministic rescue from resampling gains and provides an operational bound for policies that limit model calls.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The complete preregistration (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001; preregistration SHA‑256 = 425cb1652354120cf48f686b964723d64c76d0a8abe53cd5b5ad0eaa1af71fc7) fixed the primary estimand: the absolute paired difference in the unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded minus baseline) on paired cases that reuse the same shared_initial candidate. Confirmatory elements frozen prior to execution included planned analyzable pairs N = 300 (100 per difficulty stratum), inclusion/exclusion rules, the binary scoring rule (unflagged == pass), and the analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). The preregistration described an optional pilot (n = 60) for discordance estimation; that pilot was not executed and no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed. This explicit deviation is recorded in the preregistration archive and reiterated here for reader clarity.

Task generation and synthetic suite. Tasks were produced deterministically by the registered task generator into a synthetic_topology_suite and stratified by generator metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count). Representative difficulty patterns include shutdown_configure_restore (medium) and paired_link_atomic_mtu_change (hard). Every task manifest records required_sequences, intent constraints, protected interfaces, and preserve_unspecified_state invariants; the deterministic validator checks these properties.

Shared_initial protocol and generator. To implement the shared_initial estimand, the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial generation per pair and reused that identical candidate for both baseline and guarded conditions. The declared generator for shared_initial candidate production was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records requested_model = "gpt-5-mini"). This protocol intentionally conditions the estimand on a single LLM draw and therefore excludes any verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation). That distinction is operationally relevant when model calls are constrained by cost, latency, or governance.

Validator, scoring, and repair operator. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implements the preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation rule: deterministic checks for sequencing invariants (must_be_down_for_fields), required_command_count, preservation of unspecified state, encoded reachability invariants, and forbidden‑template protection (protected_interfaces). Scoring is binary (unflagged == pass). The guarded pipeline permitted at most one automated repair attempt (repair budget ≤1). The repair routine is a constrained edit operator limited to localized sequencing or insertion edits; it is applied only if the validator flags the shared_initial candidate and logs a repair provider trace. A candidate remaining flagged after the permitted repair counts as a failure for the primary estimand.

Contamination controls, negative controls, and stopping rules. Contamination controls included one intentionally broken negative control per complexity stratum and deterministic invariant checks (pre/post reachability matrices). Per preregistration, pairs with both calls failing due to provider/infrastructure outages would be excluded; none occurred. The preregistration also specified halting if >20% dual‑call exclusions occurred; that did not trigger during the run.

Execution instrumentation and audit. The confirmatory run used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter in scientific_confirmatory mode. Execution audit values (execution manifest): planned_episode_count = 600, completed_episode_count = 600, complete_pair_count = 300, model_calls_used = 301, maximum_model_calls = 600. Provider call auditing recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 301 and stage_counts showing shared_initial_generation = 300 and repair = 1. Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode and provider‑call accounting and reports all_deterministic_consistency_checks_passed = true. These deterministic audit values are archived to permit third‑party verification of accounting and stage counts.
sections.results:
Execution integrity and accounting. The hosted adapter completed the confirmatory run (started_at_utc 2026-08-30T09:47:41.113164+00:00, completed_at_utc 2026-08-30T10:17:21.408465+00:00). Accounting: completed_episode_count = 600, complete_pair_count = 300, model_calls_used = 301 (300 shared_initial generations + 1 repair). Provider audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 301, cache_miss_count = 301, repair stage_count = 1. Analysis artifacts confirm consistency of episode, pair, and provider accounting.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. Condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 299/300 (0.9966666666666667), guarded successes = 300/300 (1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided test returned p = 1.0. Absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0033333333333332993. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000) is [0.00, 0.01].

Per‑stratum outcomes. Stratum breakdown recorded in the analysis artifacts: low stratum (100 pairs): baseline 100/100, guarded 100/100; medium (100): baseline 100/100, guarded 100/100; high (100): baseline 99/100, guarded 100/100. Table 1 summarizes these per‑stratum counts and marginal rates.

Repair diagnostic. The single discordant episode (n10 = 1) invoked the allowed automated repair. Validator traces attribute the initial flag to an omitted sequencing command required by the intent (a must_be_down_for_fields violation): the shared_initial candidate omitted the requisite 'admin down' prior to a VLAN/MTU change. The constrained repair inserted the missing sequencing command and the deterministic validator subsequently reported valid == true. The archived run bundle contains the low‑level repair provider trace and the validator trace for this episode; the manuscript reports a concise semantic summary here rather than reproducing full provider transcripts in the body.

Contamination and missingness. The contamination_summary.csv is empty and missingness_summary.csv shows no excluded or failed episodes (all zeros for failed and unscorable episodes). No pairs were excluded under the preregistered rules and no provider/infrastructure outage exclusions occurred during the confirmatory run.

Statistical interpretation. The near‑ceiling baseline produced a single discordant pair, limiting inferential sensitivity: an exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0 reflects the paucity of discordant evidence under the shared_initial estimand. The bootstrap CI bounds plausible absolute paired improvement at ≤1 percentage point in this experimental context. These inferences apply strictly to the preregistered estimand, the fixed repair budget (≤1), the synthetic topology suite sampled by the deterministic task generator, and the declared generator (gpt-5-mini).
sections.discussion:
Estimand and operational alignment. Conditioning on a single LLM draw per intent (shared_initial) corresponds to operational policies that limit model calls (cost, latency, governance). Under such policies the guarded pipeline measures only deterministic validator and bounded repair rescue applied to the same candidate. Workflows allowing resampling, verifier‑guided generation, or interactive steering change the estimand and typically increase achievable success rates because they exploit generator variance; such workflows should be evaluated under a different preregistered estimand that permits independent alternate draws.

Ceiling effects and the unexecuted pilot. The preregistration targeted detection of a 10 percentage‑point absolute improvement with planned power ≈0.8, relying on a pilot to estimate discordance. Because the optional pilot (n = 60) intended to estimate discordance was not executed, the main run confronted a near‑ceiling baseline (299/300) producing minimal discordance (m = 1) and reduced power to detect small absolute differences. This operational lesson supports performing small calibration pilots when generator performance on a chosen task suite may be near ceiling.

Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The observed single failure mode was a sequencing omission; other classes (reachability violations, forbidden ACL removal) were not observed at scale on this synthetic suite. The marginal utility of a guarded pipeline therefore depends on (a) the deployment distribution of failure modes and (b) validator expressiveness. A richer validator or a synthetic distribution biased toward reachability or ACL invariants could increase observed rescue rates. Conversely, if operator risk policies disallow automated edits, the guarded pipeline's deterministic rescue becomes operationally limited to detection and human escalation.

Repair budget and bounded edits. We purposely limited automated repair to a single constrained edit to measure bounded deterministic rescue. That design measured only localized sequencing corrections; iterative repair, larger edit operators, or interactive verifier‑guided generation would increase rescue opportunities but test a different estimand. The archived repair trace for the single rescued episode allows detailed follow‑up analyses of repair patterns and edit efficacy.

Threats to validity. Internal validity risks include prompt sensitivity, generator nondeterminism under alternative temperature settings, and conditioning on a single draw. Construct validity concerns whether the binary unflagged scoring rule and the synthetic validator accurately represent operational risk. External validity is limited by evaluating a single model (gpt-5-mini), one validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and a synthetic task suite; results may differ on production topologies, other LLMs, or richer validators. Conclusion validity is constrained by the low discordant count; small absolute effects below the bootstrap CI upper bound cannot be excluded.

Operational recommendation. Organizations should align the evaluation estimand with operational constraints: if policies permit multiple model calls or interactive steering, allow resampling or verifier‑guided generation to measure rescue achievable by exploiting generator variance. If model calls are constrained, the shared_initial estimand provides an operationally meaningful upper bound for deterministic verifier/repair rescue applied to a single candidate.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired comparison between a verifier‑assisted pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) and accepting a single‑shot LLM candidate under the shared_initial estimand on 300 synthetic NetOps intents using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Baseline single‑shot generation produced 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, yielding an absolute paired improvement of 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). Deterministic validator+repair rescued a single sequencing omission under the bounded repair budget. The near‑ceiling baseline limits inferential sensitivity to small absolute improvements under the shared_initial estimand. All preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts are archived to enable reproducibility and targeted follow‑up studies that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, task distribution, or repair budget.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
